standard: REED Mk2.1 — reproduce, root-cause, fix the earliest broken layer, verify, regression-protect

items.title: empty initial roster
items.reproduced: The board auto-started a run on mount, so five players appeared without the user rolling.
items.rootCause: ChaosClash called start() from a mount effect.
items.fix: The board opens EMPTY with ten empty slots and a ROLL 1 button; the run is created by that press.
items.verification: Browser: THREE ROLLS AVAILABLE, 10 empty slots, 0 hold controls, ERA HIDDEN.

items.title: off-by-one roll count
items.rootCause: The unbidden first roster was counted as Roll 1, so the counter never matched what the user had done.
items.fix: The first visible roster IS Roll 1 and follows an explicit action.
items.verification: Browser: empty → ROLL 1 OF 3 → ROLL 2 OF 3 → locked.

items.title: single-player hold limitation
items.reproduced: Multi-select was exercised directly in a browser at Roll 1: three independent holds all registered, none disabled.
items.evidence: aria-pressed flipped to true on three separate cards with no control disabled.
items.explanation: The owner's experience is fully explained by 8B-04: at Roll 2 every control was disabled, which presents exactly as 'holding one player prevents another'.
items.regressionTest: scripts/chaos/holdQa.mjs covers every cardinality from zero to five

items.title: hold unavailable after Roll 2
items.reproduced: After submitting Roll 1 holds, all five hold controls reported disabled: true.
items.rootCause: The era reveal was a blocking step (busy = busy || showEra) whose acknowledge button sat below the fold, so the entire board was inert until it was found and pressed.
alternatives: A per-card interaction bug — REJECTED: multi-hold worked at Roll 1 with identical code.
A server rejection — REJECTED: no request was made; the controls were disabled client-side.
items.fix: The era became a persistent banner rather than a gate. The board is live the moment Roll 2 lands.
items.verification: Browser: every control enabled immediately at Roll 2.
items.regressionTest: e2e/phase8a-chaos.spec.js asserts no hold control is disabled at Roll 2

items.title: hold state lost between rounds
items.reproduced: A card held through Roll 1 returned at Roll 2 with aria-pressed false.
items.rootCause: Pending holds were reset to an empty array after each submission.
items.impact: Silent data loss: a user who did not re-hold a kept card burned it.
items.fix: Pending holds are seeded from the server's held slots, so kept cards start selected.
items.verification: Browser: the three cards held at Roll 1 were pre-selected at Roll 2.

items.title: held-player release behaviour
items.fix: A pre-selected card can be released; it is then burned and replaced on the next roll.
items.verification: Browser: releasing a held card flipped it to unheld and it was replaced.

items.title: final roster lock
items.rootCause: After Roll 3 the cards still read HELD and kept their controls, implying a fourth roll existed.
items.fix: Locked cards read FINAL ROSTER and no hold control is rendered.
items.verification: Browser: FINAL ROSTER present, zero player hold controls.

items.title: server validation of submitted holds
items.fix: Duplicate slots, unknown slots and non-arrays are refused without mutating the run.

items.title: CPU hold parity
items.fix: Unchanged from 8A: the CPU draws from the same model and its holds are committed before the user's are accepted.

items.title: active-run resume and logo navigation
items.rootCause: The component started a NEW run on every mount, so navigating away and back minted a fresh opening roster.
items.fix: The active run id is stored locally and resumed via a read-only view; an abandoned or simulated run is not resumed.
items.verification: A reload resumes the run in place rather than drawing a new one.

items.title: explicit abandonment
items.fix: Abandon This Draft asks for confirmation, marks the server run ABANDONED without minting a new seed, and the run can never be advanced again.

items.title: roster-summary missing fields
items.reproduced: The owner's screenshot showed Gold with five rows and Blue with four; Blue had no Biggest risk.
items.rootCause: The renderer dropped a row whose value was null.
items.fix: One schema for both sides with truthful neutral values; no row is ever removed and no weakness is invented.
items.verification: Browser: both panels show all five rows, with 'No standout strength' and 'No critical weakness identified' where they apply.

items.title: era visibility
items.rootCause: The era appeared once in a reveal panel and then only as a small line on one postgame tab.
items.fix: One EraContextBanner carried through every screen from the reveal onward, plus an ERA IMPACT line in the postgame.

items.title: three-roll Coach Draft
items.fix: Coach selection is now three offer slots, three rolls, holds and burns, then one hire — mirroring the player draft.
items.verification: Browser: COACH ROLL 1/2/3 then CHOOSE YOUR COACH; a held staff persisted across a roll.

items.title: coach offer probability
items.rootCause: Offers were the argmax per role, so the same roster always drew the same three coaches and there was no draft in the coach draft.
items.fix: Weighted sampling on fit, so better fit raises probability without guaranteeing selection.
items.verification: 600 offer sets: zero repeated offensive identities, zero duplicate coaches, all 30 coaches reachable (argmax reached about three).

items.title: coach offer diversity
items.rootCause: Novelty was a weighting preference, so two offers could still print the same offensive identity — the owner's screenshot showed two staffs both described as a transition offense.
items.fix: Distinctness is a filter on offensive identity, relaxing only when no eligible coach brings a fresh one.

items.title: CPU coach parity and no peeking
items.fix: The CPU drafts under the same rules with holds committed first, and chooses from pregame information only.

items.title: box-score stat wrapping
items.reproduced: The owner's screenshot showed 40-79, 38-79 and 21-28 broken across two lines.
items.rootCause: A fixed table layout with percentage column widths gave the made-attempted columns less width than their widest real value, and only the player cell was nowrap.
items.fix: Pair columns get their own wider track, all columns use pixel widths, and every cell is nowrap.
items.verification: Browser: zero wrapped cells; the totals row reads 37-78, 5-13, 14-22 on one line.

items.title: box-score column alignment
items.fix: Unchanged from 8A: one table, one colgroup, two row groups.
items.verification: Browser: gold and blue cell offsets identical.

items.title: quarter-story depth
items.reproduced: Each quarter carried a single line of the form 'X led the period with N'.
items.fix: Two or three real events per quarter — runs with the player who carried them, defensive stands, mismatches, ball movement, lead swings — in chronological order with quarter phase and score state.
items.verification: Measured over 48 quarters: 100% carry at least two events; 659 quarter-story checks pass over 24 games.

items.title: enhanced analysis request
items.rootCause: See enhanced-analysis-root-cause.json. Narrative validation rejected every recap because only the final score was an allowed N-N string; a real quarter score or shooting line was treated as a fabrication.
items.fix: The allowed set is every score the record contains. Invented scores and totals are still rejected, and single-digit fabrications are now caught too.
items.verification: Traced on the deployed preview (503 MODEL_CONTRADICTED_RESULT x3 then MODEL_UNAVAILABLE), then proven in isolation against the validator.

items.title: enhanced analysis polling
items.evidence: The deployed responses were 503, never a hanging 202. The Phase 8A state machine already polls 202 to a bounded conclusion and its nine tests still pass.
items.note: The spinner no longer hangs; the feature was failing for a different reason, now fixed under 8B-21.

items.title: enhanced analysis fallback
items.fix: A deterministic Expanded Game Analysis is computed from the record and shown whenever a validated provider recap is unavailable, labelled DETERMINISTIC_EXPANDED and described on screen as built from the game's own record rather than AI-assisted.

items.title: coaching report density
items.fix: Three sub-sections (Offensive Scheme, Defensive Scheme, In-Game Adjustments) behind a tablist, replacing two very long parallel columns.

items.title: adjustment repetition
items.reproduced: The owner's screenshot showed the same 'hidden defender' line four times for one coach.
items.fix: A recurring trigger and response is grouped into one line with its count and period span; at most four are shown before an explicit expand.
items.verification: Sampled games show four grouped lines per coach where eight repetitive ones stood before; a test asserts no trigger+response pair appears twice.

items.title: adjustment time labelling
items.fix: Every adjustment carries quarter phase and score state, mapped through the possession ledger. No raw possession index and no fabricated clock is shown.

items.title: targeted-matchup integration
items.fix: Folded into the Offensive Scheme as PRIMARY MATCHUPS TARGETED, always with the points it produced.

items.title: draft-shaped-game removal
items.fix: The section and all five cards are gone from the postgame; the draft history remains on the result for replay, challenges and analytics.
items.verification: Browser: absent. No renamed replacement exists.

items.title: Before Tipoff removed by a block edit
items.reproduced: The Phase 7B e2e failed on a missing BEFORE TIPOFF heading.
items.rootCause: Removing the draft-shaped block also deleted the adjacent StoredPregameRead render. The component-integrity test catches undefined references, not a deleted usage.
items.fix: Restored, plus a test that asserts StoredPregameRead is actually rendered rather than merely defined.

items.title: final-tab story hierarchy
items.fix: Unchanged from 8A and still first on the Final tab: a deterministic, player-centered 'How X Won' that never leads with the stored outlook.

items.title: era presence in postgame
items.fix: An ERA IMPACT line on the Final tab and an era line heading Coaching & Strategy, both factual and neither claiming the era decided the result.

items.title: responsive layout
items.fix: Empty slots, coach offers and the coaching sub-sections all stack on narrow viewports; the box score scrolls inside its own container.

items.title: accessibility
items.fix: Hold controls remain at least 44px with aria-pressed and a name that changes between Hold and Release; the coaching sub-sections are a real tablist; the era banner is a labelled region.

items.title: preview preservation
items.fix: No change to the access gate, keys, feedback or namespaces.
items.regressionTest: npm run preview:preflight · preview:security · wave1 deployed access check

items.title: production isolation
items.fix: No production namespace write, no merge to main, Chaos still flag-gated off in production.
